sampling_model.design: Known history-predictable randomization \(p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})\) on ordered enrollment positions.
sampling_model.units: The typed unit-level potential-outcome schedule encodes no cross-unit interference, the observation map \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{bi}=Y_{bi}(Z_{bi})\) encodes consistency, block membership is fixed, and assignment is the experiment's only endogenous randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: The shared control is available in every block, while the focal arm has positive propensity exactly on the proper block window \(W\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every available arm has compatible-history propensity at least \(p_{\min}>0\); structural zeros off the availability set are allowed, and information is averaged under the induced assignment law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Outcome regressions \(m_{bi}(z)\) are bounded and predictable; validity does not require consistency of these regressions.
sampling_model.procedure_randomization: A schedule-independent Markov kernel may use an auxiliary \(U_{\mathrm{aux}}\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) independent of the assignment experiment; coverage and expected length are computed under that same extended law. The concurrent-only subclass observes all assignment and realized propensity metadata but no outcome outside \(W\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The two-stage adding-arm simulations compare all-control and concurrent-only analyses under linear and step trends, and the stage-adjusted analysis is equivalent to concurrent-only analysis while linear adjustment can fail under nonlinear drift.

Equation (3) writes the two-period regression estimator as a concurrent-control mean plus a weighted nonconcurrent trend adjustment, and Section 3.1.2 gives unbiasedness under equal additive arm trends.

Theorem 3 gives the efficient influence function for the concurrent average treatment effect, and Section 6 finds no first-order doubly robust NCC efficiency gain when availability is deterministic in entry time.
Theorem 4 proves design-unbiasedness and a martingale central limit theorem for finite-population AIPW under adaptive randomization with positive propensity for every analyzed treatment.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 optimize honest confidence intervals through convex-class modulus and worst-case bias geometry in a Gaussian regression experiment.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds the expected length of every honest interval by a between-class Gaussian modulus and constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals over convex classes.
The paper selects data-adaptive external-control weights to keep estimated expected bias below a prespecified cap and reports bootstrap Wald inference under model-based assumptions.

Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and an attaining upper construction in a Gaussian RCT-plus-observational model with bounded scalar confounding bias; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility.

Definitions 2.1--2.3 define a concurrently randomized cohort by a common allocation design, define nonconcurrent controls by membership outside that cohort, and distinguish contemporaneous controls by same-stage enrollment.

The paper compares categorical fixed-effect, mixed-effect, and spline calendar-time adjustments for platform-trial nonconcurrent controls through simulation-based type-I-error and power analysis, finding spline control for sufficiently smooth trends and period fixed effects most robust for arbitrary equal-across-arm trends.

body.tldr: A cumulative-discrepancy linear program gives the exact worst-case bias from borrowing nonconcurrent controls, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope.  Projection yields an everywhere-nonempty, uniformly design-honest interval with worst-case expected length at most twice the clipped optimized radius.  For every adaptive design, all honest observed-data interval kernels also obey the mixture-modulus lower bound \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\).  An explicit three-block rare-history sequence proves that no positive alpha-only constant can compare this minimax length to the predictable inverse-propensity radius over the unrestricted primitive class: the radius stays at \(2M\) while an honest variable-length interval has expected length tending to zero.  A matching comparison is nevertheless proved on a computable adaptive masked-weight subclass: there must be a set of focal-window positions with target weight \(w\), enough that \(2Mw\) dominates the optimized radius, which the all-zero adaptive tree avoids assigning to the focal arm with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\).  On this class, \(\eta_\alpha\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\); avoiding the focal arm throughout the window is a simple sufficient special case.  The KKT borrowing certificate and the accepted boundary results remain distinct: zero drift licenses information-optimal full borrowing, while vacuous drift equates full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel values only under structural invariance of propensities to off-window outcomes.  The separate enumerated one-unit three-block experiment retains its certified zero-drift minimax value \(0.7M\); no positive-drift value is inferred from it.

project_justification.gap: Platform-control papers study parametric or semiparametric calendar adjustment through bias, type-I error, power, or superpopulation efficiency, while Gaussian convex-class work gives minimax expected-length theory in nonadaptive observation experiments.  None supplies a fixed-schedule randomization theorem that distinguishes a universally honest predictable-AIPW upper radius from the smaller expected length achievable by variable-length intervals when severe propensities occur only on rare adaptive histories.  The unrestricted alpha-only equivalence is therefore not merely absent from the literature; it is false.
project_justification.niche: The note treats the adaptive assignment tree itself as part of the experiment.  It combines the exact support function of the bounded-total-variation control-mean class with actual-history martingale information, an all-kernel observed-law mixture modulus, and a finite-tree reachability certificate.  This separates three objects that model-based analyses conflate: the causal finite-population contrast, an implementable honest AIPW radius, and the minimax expected length over all observed-data interval kernels.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is a sharp bias dual, a convex-program projected interval with worst-case expected length at most twice its clipped radius, a generic all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound, an explicit rare-history impossibility for any unrestricted alpha-only radius comparison, and a matching radius sandwich on the structurally restricted adaptive subclass having enough target weight on a set of positions whose focal assignments are masked with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\) along the zero-outcome tree.  The existing optimizer certificate characterizes strict gain over the concurrent AIPW rule, and the enumerated one-unit three-block problem retains its exact zero-drift primal--dual value \(0.7M\).  At the endpoints, zero drift removes the borrowing bias, whereas vacuous drift gives equality with the concurrent-only all-kernel benchmark only when propensity updates are structurally unchanged by off-window potential-outcome changes holding assignments and window outcomes fixed.

body.related_work: LeeWason2020, BofillRoigEtAl2022, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift analyze all-control versus concurrent-only platform analyses under specified linear, step, fixed-effect, mixed-effect, or spline time models and emphasize bias, type-I error, and power.  MarschnerSchou2024 defines concurrency through randomized cohorts, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 studies a superpopulation efficiency problem for the concurrent estimand.  Those results motivate the platform setting but do not give uniform fixed-schedule coverage over a total-variation drift class or minimax expected length over schedule-independent observed-data kernels.  LiZhao2026 supplies the predictable-AIPW martingale template; here the assignment law is retained schedule by schedule, so a rare branch contributes through both its probability and its inverse propensity.  ChenLiZhangYe2025, ArmstrongKolesar2018, and CaiLow2004 provide Gaussian bias--variance and mixture-modulus analogies, but their likelihood geometry cannot justify an unrestricted comparison after outcomes feed back into later assignment probabilities.  The present rare-history construction proves that such a comparison is false for the primitive adaptive class.  The positive replacement uses a different, directly verifiable experiment feature: a sufficiently probable zero-outcome subtree on which the focal arm is not reached at a set of positions carrying target weight \(w\).  Two bounded fixed schedules then agree on that subtree and differ by \(2Mw\) in the target, yielding the required total-variation certificate whenever that separation dominates the optimized radius.  AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 give bounded finite-population minimax benchmarks without staggered availability, bounded calendar drift, or this adaptive-tree obstruction.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The optimized predictable-AIPW radius is a valid constructive upper scale, but it is not the unrestricted minimax expected-length scale.  The counterexample exploits the distinction between a second-moment interval that pays for a rare low-propensity branch and a variable-length procedure that can spend part of its allowed miscoverage on that branch.  The masked-weight reachability condition is sufficient and exactly computable by finite recursion and finite subset search, but it is not claimed necessary and is most relevant when appreciable target weight lies on weakly reached focal positions.  Outside that subclass, the generic lower object remains the observed-law mixture modulus rather than the AIPW radius.  The vacuous-drift reduction separately requires propensity invariance across schedules when only off-window outcomes change; mere predictability does not imply that invariance.
body.honest_scope: The causal target remains the window-weighted finite-population arm-versus-control contrast, and assignment is the only source of experimental randomness.  The projected AIPW interval is uniformly honest for every design satisfying the primitive support, boundedness, and drift conditions, with no score-consistency or asymptotic-normality assumption.  The all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound is also generic.  No universal alpha-only equivalence between that interval's optimized radius and minimax expected length is claimed: an explicit admissible three-block sequence refutes it while maintaining a positive propensity floor in every experiment.  Matching constants are asserted only after finding a set of focal-window positions whose target weight \(w\) satisfies \(2Mw\ge\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\) and which the all-zero adaptive tree avoids assigning to the focal arm with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\); the proof constructs the two schedule-supported testing laws explicitly.  Taking the whole window is a simpler sufficient special case.  The KKT result compares NCC and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not the two all-kernel minimax values.  At zero drift, equal control block means remove borrowing bias and permit information-optimal use of all blocks.  At vacuous drift, full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel minimax values coincide only under the accepted structural condition that propensity updates are invariant to off-window potential-outcome changes with assignments and window outcomes fixed.  The separate finite three-block LP asserts only its proved zero-drift value \(0.7M\), supported by matching primal and dual certificates.  No claim is made that the drift budget is identified from trial data, that the masked-weight condition is necessary, or that the finite LP has the same value at positive drift.
